resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) on resale
resale_co.issued_by: Edgewater Building Department (Construction Official as Enforcement Officer)
resale_co.lead_time: Code says the inspection is done within a reasonable time, not more than 30 days after a complete application. Residential CCO inspections are Tuesday and Thursday, 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM.
requirements: Apply before the sale; no one may occupy the home after a sale until the CCO is issued
Proof of paid taxes must be shown before the certificate is issued
Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms within 10 feet of all sleeping areas on every level
Carbon monoxide detectors on every level, within 10 feet of sleeping areas, outside any room with a fuel-burning appliance and near an attached garage entrance
Handrails on all stairways with three or more risers
Must meet Hotel and Multiple Dwelling Law items (holes in walls, GFIs, paint)
Portable ABC fire extinguisher no larger than 10 pounds in or near the kitchen for 1 and 2 family homes (Borough code still lists it)
A separate Fire Prevention Bureau Certificate of Compliance is also required for sales

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in and print the Commercial / Residential Certificate of Continued Occupancy application and bring it, with the fee and proof of paid taxes, to the Building Department, 55 River Road, Second Floor, Room 223. Someone must be at the home for the inspection (Tuesday or Thursday, 11 AM to 2 PM). Apply separately to the Fire Prevention Bureau for the sale Certificate of Compliance.

resale_co.notes: Borough Code Chapter 157, Article III (Certificates of Continued Occupancy) was read through the ecode360 print view. Ordinance 2026-002 (adopted March 16, 2026) replaced the old fees ($50 one family, $75 two family, $25 reinspection, still shown on ecode360) with separate Building Department and Fire Prevention Bureau sale inspection fees. The Building Department form still shows a flat $100.00 residential CCO fee and a $50.00 re-inspection fee, so the two family amount ($125) should be confirmed. The Building Department form header lists ext. 3126; the department page lists 943-1700 ext. 3127 for the Construction Official. Rental CCOs and the annual $100 non-owner-occupied registration are rental items, not resale items.

requirements: Smoke alarms placed by year built: pre-1977 homes on each level and within 10 feet of sleeping areas (10-year sealed battery allowed); newer homes need 110V interconnected alarms as originally required
Any smoke alarm more than 10 years old must be replaced; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed, UL or ETL listed
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of all sleeping areas, on every level, outside any room with a fuel-burning appliance and near an attached garage entrance
CO detectors more than 5 years old must be replaced unless the maker allows longer (10 years for sealed combination units)
A COC is only issued once all open building permits are closed and all taxes, penalties and fees owed to the Borough are paid
No one may occupy the home before Fire Prevention Bureau approval

fire_cert.notes: The Fire Prevention Bureau runs a separate sale Certificate of Compliance under Ord. 157-10 and N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3. The application form shows a flat $100 fee; Ordinance 2026-002 sets $100 for one family and $125 for two family Fire Prevention Bureau sale inspections, so confirm the two family amount. No days-before-closing fee tiers are published. The sale form does not list a fire extinguisher, but Borough Code 157-6F (for the Building Department CCO) still does, although the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19). Fire Official email stevenc@edgewaternj.org is from the NJ DCA fire directory (survey 5/18/2026); the directory lists (201) 943-1700 for him.

other_items.label: Paid taxes
other_items.detail: Proof of paid taxes must be shown before the Building Department issues the CCO, and the Fire Prevention COC needs all taxes, penalties and fees owed to the Borough paid.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: The Fire Prevention Certificate of Compliance is only issued once all open building permits are closed.

open_questions: Which CCO fee applies for a two family sale: the $100 on the Building Department form or $125 under Ordinance 2026-002?
Does the Building Department still require a fire extinguisher (Code 157-6F) after P.L.2025, c.19?
Are there faster-service fee tiers for the Fire Prevention certificate when closing is near? None are published.
